title: How to use AI for sales prospecting
description: Find customers who fit for a reason: start from your best customers, search where the real signals are, and check a small sample before scaling.
introduction: Most AI prospecting tools hand you a list pulled from the same database everyone else uses. You get names and a score, then spend the afternoon working out which ones are real.

A better result is a smaller list where you can see why each company is on it. Strawberry gets there by learning what a good customer looks like for you, searching the places where the evidence actually lives, and checking a sample with you before it scales.

sections.title: Start from your best customers, not a perfect ICP

blocks.text: You don't need a polished ideal customer profile to begin. Your website, your CRM, the deals you won, and the ones that went nowhere already say a lot about who you sell to. Strawberry can read those, with your permission, instead of asking you to write it all down.
Tell it what you're unsure about and what to rule out, like existing customers, competitors, or regions you don't serve. Rough is fine. The first sample will sharpen it.

items.context: Describe who you sell to, or let Strawberry learn it from your website and CRM, and get a first sample with a reason for each prospect.

blocks.text: The companies worth calling often show up at the edges of the web: a niche directory, a job post for the role your product replaces, a funding announcement, a public register, a new office opening. A shared lead database rarely has any of that.

Because Strawberry works in a real browser, it can open those sources, follow the links, and keep digging when the first page comes up short. On LinkedIn it works at a human pace and stops on warnings, so your account stays safe.

sections.title: Check a small sample before scaling

blocks.text: The first run is deliberately small and varied, with a couple of borderline cases in it. You say what feels right and what doesn't, and the criteria get sharper before any real time or credits go into a wider search.

Then you choose the shape of the bigger run. A wide pass screens many companies on lighter signals. A deep pass researches fewer companies properly. Often the best answer is both: screen wide, then go deep on the ones that matter.
Every prospect comes with enough to decide in a few seconds whether it belongs:

rows: Who it is, with a link
One line tied to your criteria
A reason to reach out now, when there is one
Whether it is in your CRM or on an existing list

blocks.text: If too few companies meet the bar, Strawberry says so and offers options, like widening a criterion or trying other sources. It doesn't quietly pad the list to hit a number.

From there, your companion can research the strongest accounts more deeply, fill in the contacts you need, make a one-pager for a specific account, or draft outreach in your voice. Finding, adding to the CRM, drafting, and sending are separate steps, and nothing goes out without your say.
Once the search works, save it as a skill so the next one starts from what you've already agreed. Share it with your team, or turn it into a Routine that looks for new companies every week.
